notes:
**S175-notes.** The page gives a topological picture behind equisingularity over the complex base field, under the simplifying phrase “en supposant pour fixer les idées”. It describes a tubular neighbourhood T retracting onto X_0, local triviality of the pair, a boundary fibration, and a fibrewise cone model. It explicitly writes the attaching face as x mapped to (x,1), then the punctured part as \(\mathring T=T-X_0\simeq\partial T\times[0,1[\), and claims an X_0-homotopy to the boundary. The smoothness assertion is conditional: “Si X_0 et X_1 sont non singuliers”. It further claims that the inclusion of the modified X_1 is a homotopy equivalence and reconstructs X from the displayed span “à homéomorphisme près”. No explicit authorial doubt or question mark occurs here; transcription doubts are editorial.

The narrow checks have explicit limits. Given the displayed quotient with its t=1 face attached to X_0, deletion of X_0 leaves the parameter interval [0,1[ (**S175-cone-endpoint**, readers B/C). On that product, H_s(b,t)=(b,(1-s)t) remains in the interval, fixes t=0 and preserves p(b), proving the stated homotopy over X_0 under the model (**S175-product-homotopy**, readers A/B/C). These checks do not prove that the required tubular neighbourhood exists.

There is also a literal boundary compatibility problem (**S175-boundary-inclusion**, readers A/B/C and main). In that same model, the outer boundary copy at t=0 belongs to T-X_0. The written definition \(\widetilde X_1=X_1-\mathring T\) removes it, whereas the following diagram labels the map from that boundary into \(\widetilde X_1\) as an inclusion. For a nonempty boundary copy, these literal identifications require an additional interior/collar convention that the page does not state. This is a local compatibility finding, not a refutation of the intended gluing construction. The definition crop clearly shows the minus and ringed T; neither was repaired. Likewise, “T sur X” is preserved: the second X is unindexed even though the displayed gluing projection targets X_0 (**S175-cone-base**, reader B; a visual comparison of written bases, recorded as background rather than a mathematical check).

Root resolves the first small arrow from its closed terminal loop, but retains the two weaker relation endings. The diagram keeps both comparisons as two waves over a line, the horizontal letter above its arrow and inclusion below, and p right / fibration left of the downward arrow. The letter remains J/j, with J preferred from its undotted broad loop. The complete raised phrase si ∂T est le replaces the old cancellation. Cancelled dev. is readable; the neighbouring cancelled symbols remain doubtful. The acute in réconstitue, spaced au dessus and final semicolon are retained. Three detached dark marks are drawn without assigning them mathematical or textual meanings.

Author page **30**, archive pencil **175**, has no title or date. It is a continuous letter passage interrupted by its diagram. The opening phraser joins the preceding para fragment; the final plus continues the sentence on the next page. Consolidated references count 24 prose baselines and identify diagram positions separately; readers A and B used different diagram-inclusive counts, mapped in the comparison table.
